title: Standby activation quarantine and acceptance tests
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement a deterministic quarantine and acceptance testbed for warm-standby activations across regions and tiers. The goal is to reduce incorrect cutovers caused by transient telemetry noise, model-variant incompatibilities, or partially warmed KV caches. This ticket covers test scenarios, acceptance metrics, quarantine timing heuristics, an automated harness that runs synthetic traffic and checks readiness gates, and integration hooks for the routing decision engine to honor the acceptance verdict.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic quarantine window (configurable, default 30s) is enforced before promoting a standby region to active for production traffic
Acceptance gates evaluate: 95th percentile inference latency, error rate, KV cache hit ratio, model variant hash compatibility, and recent rollout success rate
Automated test harness can simulate 10 different failure/recovery scenarios and produce a pass/fail verdict reproducibly
Routing controller consumes an explicit readiness verdict endpoint and will not route >5% production traffic until acceptance criteria pass
End-to-end smoke test and a rollback path are documented and wired to the cutover runbook
tasks: Design quarantine state machine and config knobs (duration, cool-off increments, early-pass thresholds)
Define readiness metrics, thresholds and how to compute them atomically from telemetry (per-model, per-tier)
Extend canary harness to simulate synthetic KV-prefill and cold-cache scenarios
Implement deterministic variant-compatibility check that verifies tokenizer and model config hashes
Add readiness verdict API on regional priming controller and expose metrics to Console
Wire routing decision engine to respect verdicts and implement muted-traffic ramp for partial pass
Create automated integration tests and chaos scenarios for the harness
Update runbook and add cross-team announcement template
progress_updates: 2026-02-18: Kickoff with SRE, runtime and routing leads. Agreed quarantine default 30s with exponential backoff increments up to 5 minutes.
2026-02-23: Prototype readiness verdict API (GET /v1/region/{r}/readiness) implemented behind feature flag. Returns a single string verdict and per-metric labels (internal).
2026-03-01: Initial synthetic KV-prefill module implemented in the harness; simulates realistic prefix reuse patterns from customer traces.
2026-03-04: Discovered model-variant incompatibility issue when serving quantized 4-bit variant with tokenizer version mismatch. Added variant hash check to acceptance gates.

2026-03-07: Integration test for muted traffic ramp (5% -> 25% -> 100%) implemented. Observed a corner-case where error spike from third-party auth caused premature failover; added dependency check for downstream services.
2026-03-10: Feature flag rollout plan approved by Product. Preparing gated rollout to staging for runtime-1.22
review_feedback: PM review (Diane Morales): Ensure customer-facing SLAs are not weakened during quarantine; propose policy that only unserved requests are redirected during warm-up.
Design review (Luis Ortega): Console UX should surface both 'verdict' and per-metric reasons so SREs can triage. Add short links to failing metric dashboards.
Security review (Asha Mehra): No sensitive data in readiness payloads; ensure model-hash check does not expose model internals. Approved.
SRE feedback (Ravi Kapoor): Add a guard to prevent oscillation when a region flips between PASS/DEGRADED due to transient network partitions. Suggest hysteresis window equal to quarantine duration.
notes: Tradeoffs considered: aggressive early-pass reduces recovery time but increases risk of partially-warmed caches and higher error rates. We chose conservative default with easy knob for advanced customers.
We will expose quarantine duration and early-pass thresholds as tenant-level overrides for Dedicated customers behind an enterprise feature flag.
Next steps after acceptance: add historical scorecard that learns typical warmup times per-customer to accelerate future activations.
